author: Zia
text:
Dear @Joseph @Harry I have a question. Thanks in advance.

A quick question connected to the `navigator.language → currency → nationality` chain we discussed here — but for a different purpose (SEO, not nationality storage).

**Short background:** While auditing the site for SEO, we found that the "current display language" is signaled in several places that **don't agree with each other**:

| Signal | Value |
| --- | --- |
| localStorage `lang` | `ko` |
| localStorage `locale.language` | `EN` |
| `<html lang>` | `en` (hardcoded — follows neither) |
| Currency | www = KRW / m = USD |

For SEO, `<html lang>` (and page `title` / `meta`) must reflect the language the content is **actually rendered in** (e.g., Korean content → `lang="ko"`). Right now they don't, and the fact that these signals conflict suggests there may be **no single value that everything reads from**.

**Question:** Is there a single source-of-truth value (or function) in the current code that represents **"which language we are currently showing this user"**?

* **If yes** → could you tell us which variable/store it is, so `<html lang>` / `title` / `meta` can all reference it?
* **If no** (each screen/signal decides on its own) → we'll define one single display-language value and have those reference it.

This is **separate from the nationality-storage work** in this ticket — we just need to know whether that single display-language value already exists. Thanks!

author: Joseph
text:
@Mon @Harry   
#1 — Currency limitation directly conflicts with Google's price-accuracy requirement

The plan accepts as a "known limitation" (rated Medium) that the app **can't honor** `USER-CURRENCY` **independently of** `USER-LANGUAGE` — currency is forced from the language prefix (en→USD, ko→KRW, ja→JPY, vi→VND, zh→USD).

But Google's gTech answer was explicit: they convert to the user's display currency with their own FX, and _"to prevent variances from causing Price Accuracy mismatches, we highly recommend passing_ `USER-CURRENCY` _and_ `USER-LANGUAGE` _in your landing-page deep links so checkout renders in the same currency the user saw."_ The plan receives `&currency=(USER-CURRENCY)` and then drops it. That's the exact failure mode Google warned about.

Why it's higher than Medium: price accuracy is _the_ metric that drives ranking, visibility, and suspension risk (the whole premise of the ADR). And Google's accuracy crawler checks specific currency points-of-sale — so even low real-user traffic in a currency can trigger a mismatch penalty when the landing page forces the wrong currency. Concretely it breaks whenever Google's display currency ≠ the language default: e.g. `lang=en` forces USD even if Google showed JPY; `zh→USD` is also questionable for TW/HK markets.

Google handed you the interim fix in the same email: **restrict POS matching rules to native-currency-only** until the app can decouple currency from language. That caps the price-accuracy exposure at the cost of some global-auction visibility — a deliberate, Google-endorsed trade. The plan's current mitigation ("align feed currency with target-market language") is vague and doesn't actually use that lever. Recommend: adopt the matching-rule restriction now, and log it as a real backlog item to make landing-page currency independent of language.

### #2 — Cross-doc inconsistency with the updated ARI plan (fixed-price → rate plans)

The coverage report classifies `PACKAGE-ID`, `RATE-PLAN-ID`, `PARTNER-ROOM-ID`, `PROMO-CODE`, `RATE-RULE-ID` as "not applicable — ARI conditional rates / room bundles not on platform," and routes every click to the generic room-list.

That framing predates the 2026-06-22 ADR change: we now **deliberately model per-date fixed-price promotions as dedicated rate plans (PackageID)** pushed via the rate message. So "ARI rates not on platform" is no longer accurate — we _are_ the ARI partner pushing rate plans. The functional risk: if/when those fixed-price rate plans surface as room-level (`CLICK-TYPE=room`) results, a user who clicked a specific package on Google lands on the generic room-list, where that exact package price must still be visible, selectable, and matching — or it's a price/room mismatch.

This is probably fine _if_ the room-list page always renders the same rate plans at the same prices Google displayed — but that needs to be explicitly verified, not assumed. Action: confirm whether the pushed fixed-price packages can generate room-level clicks, and that `search-room-type` shows the identical rate. If yes, the generic landing is acceptable; if not, those clicks need deep-linking to the rate plan. Either way, update the report's "not on platform" wording.

author: Tom
text:
PR opened: https://github.com/ohmyhotelco/oh-admin/pull/242

**Root cause:** The upload "new slot" (`*ngIf="showNewSlot"`) renders inside the sortable container `#dropList` but is not part of the photo array, so Sortable.js computed drag indexes off-by-one and ngx-sortablejs injected an `undefined` item → blank tile + wrong saved order. After reload the new-slot is closed so indexes matched, which is why reorder worked only after reopen.

**Fix:** restrict dragging to real photo tiles (`draggable` + `filter`) in both hotel and room `photo-drag-drop` components so drag indexes match the array.

**Verified** on the running app: upload A,B,C → drag C to front → Save now persists [C, A, B] with no blank tile.
